registers.name: MEMMAP_LOW_00000002
registers.evidence_line: 0x02 – 0xFF        MIPI Reserved           Reserved for future use by the MIPI Alliance

registers.name: MEMMAP_HIGH_000000FF
registers.evidence_line: 0x02 – 0xFF        MIPI Reserved           Reserved for future use by the MIPI Alliance

base_address: Defined at SoC level; offsets given relative to module base.
notes: MIPI I3C Basic is a wire-level protocol specification, not a controller block guide. There is no SoC-level architectural register map. However, the spec defines three protocol-level characteristics registers that every device on the bus must expose (or hold virtually for I2C Slaves) — BCR, DCR, and (for legacy I2C devices) LVR.

protocol_level_characteristic_registers.name: BCR (Bus Characteristics Register)
protocol_level_characteristic_registers.applies_to: Every I3C compliant Device (Master or Slave)
protocol_level_characteristic_registers.access: Read-only via GETBCR Direct CCC (0x8E) or as part of the 8 bytes returned during ENTDAA arbitration

fields.name: Device Role[1:0]
fields.description: 00 = I3C Slave; 01 = I3C Master; 10/11 = Reserved by MIPI

fields.name: Bridge Identifier
fields.description: 0 = not a Bridge Device; 1 = is a Bridge Device (must comply with full I3C v1.0)

fields.name: Offline Capable
fields.description: 0 = always responds to I3C bus commands; 1 = may be offline (retains DA)

fields.name: IBI Payload
fields.description: 0 = no mandatory data byte follows accepted IBI; 1 = one or more mandatory data bytes follow, with T-Bit continuation

fields.name: Max Data Speed Limitation
fields.description: 0 = no limitation; 1 = limitation (Master must use GETMXDS to interrogate)

protocol_level_characteristic_registers.name: DCR (Device Characteristics Register)
protocol_level_characteristic_registers.access: Read-only via GETDCR Direct CCC (0x8F) or as part of the 8 bytes returned during ENTDAA arbitration

fields.name: Device ID[7:0]
fields.description: 255 available codes describing the type of device (e.g. accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, composite, generic). Default = 8'h00 = Generic Device.

protocol_level_characteristic_registers.name: LVR (Legacy Virtual Register)
protocol_level_characteristic_registers.applies_to: Every Legacy I2C Device on an I3C bus (held virtually by the Main Master / Application Host)
protocol_level_characteristic_registers.access: Loaded by the higher-level entity; transferable to Secondary Masters via DEFSLVS CCC (0x08)

fields.name: Legacy I2C only[2:0] (Index)
fields.description: Index into Table 5 — 3'b000 Index 0; 3'b001 Index 1; 3'b010 Index 2; 3'b011..3'b111 Reserved

fields.name: MIPI Reserved (Device-specific codes)
fields.description: 15 codes available for describing legacy I2C device capabilities / function

protocol_level_characteristic_registers.name: PID (Provisional ID)
protocol_level_characteristic_registers.applies_to: Every I3C compliant Device — burned in non-volatile / factory memory
protocol_level_characteristic_registers.access: Read-only via GETPID Direct CCC (0x8D) — returned as 6 bytes MSb-first; also driven during ENTDAA arbitration (Big-Endian)

fields.name: MIPI Manufacturer ID
fields.description: 15-bit MIPI Manufacturer ID per MIPI Alliance Manufacturer ID Page (most significant bit of the 16-bit MID is discarded)

fields.name: Provisional ID Type Selector
fields.description: 1'b0 = Vendor Fixed Value (Manufacturer-burnt); 1'b1 = Random Value (e.g. test mode)

fields.name: Instance ID
fields.description: 4-bit unique instance identifier among devices of the same Part ID on a bus

fields.name: DCR-defined / Vendor-defined
fields.description: 12-bit field whose meaning is left to the vendor / DCR-specific definition

soc_dependent_registers: Concrete I3C controller IP blocks expose their own register file (transmit/receive FIFO, status, interrupt enable, address, mode select, baud / SCL divider, IBI / Hot-Join control, error flags, BCR/DCR shadow, etc.) — these are defined per controller block guide, not by this specification.
